title: Agent OS Project Configuration
description: Created by /agent-os:setup. Read by all agents to adapt behavior to the project.

status.description: Status (Jira) or state (Plane) name, as shown on the board.

id.description: Status / state ID, when known. Plane moves by state ID.

gitConventions.description: Git conventions of one repo; each field overrides the same field of config.git.

base_branch.description: Long-lived branch feature branches are born from (e.g. qa). null = branch from the current HEAD.

branch_pattern.description: Feature branch name with placeholders {key}, {task}, {slug} (e.g. feature/{key}-{slug}). Must contain {key} or {task}.

commit_pattern.description: Commit subject when the task has an issue key. Placeholders {key}, {task}, {type}, {scope}, {summary} (e.g. '{key} | {type}: {summary}').

commit_pattern_no_key.description: Commit subject when the task has no issue key (e.g. '{type}: {summary}').

commit_types.description: Allowed commit types, in order of preference.

commit_language.description: Language of commit subjects and bodies (ISO 639-1, e.g. en).

protected_branches.description: Branches /agent-os:commit never commits on. A trailing * is a glob (release/*).

project_type.description: new = greenfield, existing = active codebase, legacy = old codebase to modernize

workspace_type.description: single = this directory is the project; monorepo = this is the git root with backend/frontend as subdirectories sharing one repo; multi-repo = backend and frontend are separate git repos inside this directory (root is not a git repo)

focus.description: Which developer roles are active. fullstack = backend-developer + frontend-developer; backend = only backend-developer (frontend subtasks are skipped); frontend = only frontend-developer (backend subtasks are skipped)

workspace_paths.description: Sub-directory paths for backend and frontend when workspace_type is monorepo or multi-repo. Paths are relative to the workspace root. Not used for single.

backend.description: Relative path from workspace root to the backend project directory.

frontend.description: Relative path from workspace root to the frontend project directory.

package_manager.description: e.g. bun, pnpm, npm, yarn, uv, pip, poetry, maven, gradle, go mod

test_command.description: Command to run the test suite

dev_command.description: Command to start the development server

build_command.description: Command to build the project for production

review_required.description: Whether human review is required before merging

track_state_in_git.description: Whether .agent-os/ files should be committed to git

require_architecture_approval.description: Whether the design stage requires explicit user approval before development

require_requirements_approval.description: Whether the discovery stage requires explicit user approval before planning

output_language.description: Language for all agent output and pipeline messages. en = English, es = Español

requirements_format.description: How Stage 1 writes functional requirements. req = REQ-NNN list (default); user-stories = US-NNN user stories with acceptance criteria. Non-functional requirements and constraints stay REQ-NNN in both formats.

approver.description: Optional approver agent that reviews stage outputs before their gates. Missing, or enabled = false: the pipeline behaves exactly as without it. The architecture gate (design) can only be given to it in unattended mode.

enabled.description: Turns the approver on for the gates listed in gates.

mode.description: advisory = the verdict is shown at a human gate and the human decides (planning gets a human gate while the approver reviews it). autonomous = APPROVE advances without asking; REQUEST_CHANGES re-runs the producing agent up to max_revisions times, then stops at a human gate. unattended = the approver also answers the clarifying questions, decides scope changes, may review the architecture, and QA failures re-run development; after max_revisions it continues with unresolved major/minor findings and stops only on a blocker. Post-QA commands tagged [gate] still ask the human.

gates.description: Gates the approver reviews. requirements (Stage 1) and planning (Stage 2) in any mode; design (Stage 3, architecture) only when mode = unattended.

items.description: requirements = requirements-approved gate; planning = plan-approved gate; design = architecture-approved gate (unattended only).

max_revisions.description: autonomous and unattended: how many revision runs a stage may get without a human (approver REQUEST_CHANGES; in unattended also QA REQUEST_CHANGES). Human change requests do not count. 0 = stop at the first REQUEST_CHANGES (autonomous only; unattended requires at least 1).

tracker.description: Optional issue tracker integration (Jira or Plane), used only by the orchestrator through the tracker-sync skill. Missing: no tracker, nothing changes. Never contains credentials.

connection.description: How agent-os talks to the tracker. Only mcp (the MCP server registered in Claude Code) is supported; a REST connection is not available yet.

mcp.description: The MCP server that exposes the tracker tools.

server.description: Name the MCP server is registered with in Claude Code (its tools are named mcp__<server>__<tool>). Tools are discovered by this prefix at run time.

mode.description: pull = take existing issues (/agent-os:start VR-123, /agent-os:tracker pick); create = agent-os creates the parent issue after the requirements and one sub-task per subtask after the plan, each after the user approves it; both = either, per task.

jira.description: Jira Cloud settings. Required when provider = jira.

cloud_id.description: Atlassian cloud ID of the site, discovered in setup (some MCP tools need it). Not a secret.

parent_type.description: Issue type of the parent issue created in create mode.

subtask_type.description: Issue type of the sub-tasks created in create mode.

role_field.description: How the developer role (backend / frontend) is written on created sub-tasks.

plane.description: Plane settings. Required when provider = plane.

base_url.description: Plane web URL, for links (self-hosted instances use their own).

workspace_slug.description: Workspace slug, as in the URL.

project_identifier.description: Project identifier used in work item keys, e.g. REACH for REACH-12.

pick_assigned_to_me.description: pick lists only the issues assigned to the current user.

status_route.description: Route of action: the tracker status each pipeline event moves the issue (and, in create mode, its sub-tasks) to. null or missing = that event does not move anything. Confirmed by the user in setup or /agent-os:tracker map.

intake.description: Status pick lists issues from (not a move), e.g. To Do.

start.description: Moved to when discovery starts on the issue, e.g. In Progress.

development.description: Moved to when development starts (sub-tasks: when their developer run starts).

done_pipeline.description: Moved to when QA approves. Usually the column before Done (e.g. Code Review), because the PR is still missing. Done only if the user mapped it.

blocked.description: Moved to when the stage becomes blocked.

git.description: Optional git conventions of the project, proposed by /agent-os:setup from the commit history and used by /agent-os:commit. Missing fields take the defaults listed in /agent-os:commit. Nothing about branches or commit formats is fixed in the plugin.

base_branch.description: Long-lived branch feature branches are born from (e.g. qa). null = branch from the current HEAD.

branch_pattern.description: Feature branch name with placeholders {key}, {task}, {slug} (e.g. feature/{key}-{slug}). Must contain {key} or {task}.

commit_pattern.description: Commit subject when the task has an issue key. Placeholders {key}, {task}, {type}, {scope}, {summary} (e.g. '{key} | {type}: {summary}').

commit_pattern_no_key.description: Commit subject when the task has no issue key (e.g. '{type}: {summary}').

commit_types.description: Allowed commit types, in order of preference.

commit_language.description: Language of commit subjects and bodies (ISO 639-1, e.g. en).

protected_branches.description: Branches /agent-os:commit never commits on. A trailing * is a glob (release/*).

repos.description: Per-repo overrides, keyed by repo path relative to the workspace root (a workspace_paths value, or '.'). Used when the repos follow different conventions.

extensions.description: Optional skill, doc, agent, and command extensions for the pipeline. Managed via /agent-os:skills. Same shape as ~/.agent-os/defaults.json (see defaults.schema.json); within each tier, project entries are applied after user entries and win on conflict.
